name: bt

profile.reading: This building at 492 River Road in Nutley, New Jersey, in Essex County, has been identified with BT Radianz, the low latency financial extranet network operated by BT Group. Radianz began as a joint venture backed by Reuters and Equant, launched in 2000 to give banks, brokerages, exchanges and other financial services firms a single shared connection for market data, order routing and trading applications, replacing the patchwork of separate leased lines that each counterparty had previously needed to maintain with every trading partner. BT, the British telecommunications group formally known as BT Group plc, acquired full ownership of Radianz in 2005 and folded it into its global financial services business under the BT Radianz name. The network's core proposition, one physical connection into a shared, secure extranet that then reaches thousands of counterparties, exchanges and market data vendors, made it a fixture of Wall Street and the wider global trading industry through the 2000s and 2010s. The Radianz brand remains active today. BT's current business division markets a product called Radianz for Finance, describing it as a secure, private network for financial organisations with customers in more than 60 countries connected through roughly 40 data centres worldwide, evidence that the underlying network infrastructure this facility was part of has continued operating and evolving rather than being discontinued. Nutley and neighboring Clifton sit in the New York metropolitan area's financial technology corridor, within reach of the exchange matching engines and financial firms clustered across northern New Jersey, a location consistent with a low latency network point of presence serving Wall Street. What could not be confirmed is whether the 492 River Road building specifically remains an operating BT Radianz point of presence today, or whether BT has since consolidated its New Jersey infrastructure into other sites as the network's footprint evolved over the two decades since the 2005 acquisition. No power capacity or floor area figure for this address was located. This entry records the Radianz network's well documented history and current commercial status honestly, while leaving the building's present day operational role at this specific address as an open question rather than an assumed fact.

reading:
BT Group plc is the United Kingdom's incumbent telecommunications carrier, listed in London as BT.A and traded in the United States only as a depositary receipt, so it files no annual report with the Securities and Exchange Commission and publishes almost nothing about individual buildings. It appears in a United States data centre registry for one reason, the site at 492 River Road in Nutley, in Essex County, New Jersey, which for years was one of the core locations of Radianz, the closed extranet BT ran for the trading industry.

Radianz was never a public internet service. It was a private financial community network that let banks, brokers, exchanges, market data vendors and clearing houses reach one another through a single connection instead of building point to point circuits, and the New Jersey site was one of the places where those connections physically met. That is why the building matters more than its floor area suggests. The property is about 130,000 square feet of secure office and data centre space, fully renovated in 2000 and updated again in 2009, with two meet me rooms, access to thirteen telecommunications providers and an on site substation described as expandable.

Two things in this record are worth stating plainly. First, BT does not own the building. GI Partners bought 492 River Road in February 2018 with BT Americas as the sole tenant on an extended long term lease, and reporting on that deal traced earlier ownership through Essex County records to Reckson Associates, part of SL Green Realty. BT is the operator of the space, not the landlord, which is the normal arrangement for a carrier point of presence and a distinction this registry tries to keep visible. Second, BT no longer runs Radianz. BT's own business pages now state that its Radianz financial solutions have been discontinued and the business sold to Transaction Network Services, a Virginia based infrastructure provider that markets Radianz inside its Waypoint trading portfolio and describes more than 6,500 connected endpoints. This research did not establish what BT retains at Nutley after that sale.

No megawatt figure of any kind has been published for this site, and none should be inferred from its square footage or from the presence of a substation on the property. A substation is utility infrastructure, and its rating, wherever one is eventually found, will not be the building's IT load. The operator type recorded here, enterprise private, also understates what BT is. Its United States presence is carrier and managed network infrastructure supporting its own service delivery and its financial customers, not colocation sold by the cabinet, and that is the right way to read the single New Jersey row.
